questions.question: What is the main focus of TR86?

options.A: Explaining basic CCI concepts for traditional containers such as stoppered glass vials, and introducing entry-level test methods and their interpretation
options.B: Exploring the challenges of complex packaging systems such as syringes and bulk containers, and innovative applications of existing technologies
options.C: Listing the CCIT methods that regulators require drug manufacturers to use, and specifying their order of use and acceptance criteria
options.D: Governing the calibration frequency and acceptance criteria of CCIT equipment, and setting personnel qualification requirements for laboratories

questions.explanation: TR86 focuses on the challenges that sterile drug products and biologics face with complex packaging systems (such as syringes, syringe assemblies, and bulk containers) and introduces innovative approaches using existing technologies. The basic concepts are already covered by TR-27 and USP <1207>, and TR86 also states explicitly that its content is a team consensus and does not necessarily represent the views of regulatory agencies.

questions.topic: Why a new report beyond TR-27
questions.question: After the PDA technical report team re-examined TR-27, why did it decide to write TR86?

options.A: To replace USP <1207> as the sole package integrity reference document and withdraw all earlier PDA reports
options.B: Because the content of TR-27 had been withdrawn by regulators and PDA had to develop a new version
options.C: To set mandatory test specifications and acceptance criteria for prefilled syringes only
options.D: To build on the updated foundation of USP <1207> and address more advanced package integrity topics

questions.explanation: The team concluded that a separate report focused on advanced topics should be written on the foundation updated by USP <1207>, such as complex systems like large-volume bulk packages and prefilled syringes, because no single source currently addresses these issues completely. TR86 supplements rather than replaces USP <1207>, and its scope is not limited to syringes.

questions.question: According to the TR86 glossary, what is the difference between deterministic and probabilistic leak test methods?

options.A: Deterministic methods rely on predictable phenomena and controllable physicochemical techniques to obtain objective quantitative data; probabilistic methods rely on events with random outcomes
options.B: Deterministic methods are always destructive; probabilistic methods are always non-destructive; the two are not interchangeable
options.C: Deterministic methods can only detect the presence or absence of a leak; only probabilistic methods give a quantitative leak rate, leak location, and defect geometry
options.D: Deterministic methods are used only for rigid containers; probabilistic methods only for flexible containers; the two cannot be used across types

questions.explanation: In deterministic methods, leak events follow a predictable chain of cause and effect, and measurement is based on controllable and monitorable physicochemical techniques that yield objective quantitative data; probabilistic methods are random in nature, and results are described by probability distributions. Whether a method is destructive and whether the container is rigid or flexible are not what defines the two.

questions.question: How does TR86 define the Maximum Allowable Leak Limit (MALL)?

options.A: The smallest leak size that a test instrument can detect in the laboratory
options.B: The maximum reject rate of containers that can be removed on the production line
options.C: The maximum gap or leak rate that does not put product quality at risk
options.D: The smallest defect orifice size at which a positive control can be made

questions.explanation: The MALL is the maximum gap or leak rate that can be tolerated without affecting product quality, and it is determined by product quality requirements. "The smallest leak size that a test instrument can detect" describes the limit of detection (LoD), which is different: the LoD is a method capability, whereas the MALL is a product requirement.

questions.question: Which of the following best matches the TR86 definition and scope of package integrity?

options.A: Only the ability to prevent liquid product from leaking out of the container, not including ingress of gases or microorganisms
options.B: The ability to prevent product loss or maintain sterility, including maintaining the internal environment (such as a vacuum seal)
options.C: A dimensional attribute of packaging materials assessed only at finished product release, excluding performance over shelf life and the ability to maintain the environment
options.D: Packaging materials meeting tensile and compressive strength requirements during transport, without involving seal performance

questions.explanation: Package integrity is the ability of the packaging to prevent product loss, maintain product sterility, and maintain the internal environment (for example, loss of a vacuum seal). The report also stresses that it is an ongoing process that starts with packaging development and runs through the whole product life cycle, not something done once at release.

questions.question: Why does TR86 state that naturally occurring leaks should not be used for validation of CCIT methods?

options.A: Because there are too many of them to track one by one, and the location of each defect cannot be confirmed
options.B: Because regulators do not accept real defects as controls and accept only artificially created defects
options.C: Because they vary widely, the leak size and geometry are often unknown, and they are easily blocked by product
options.D: Because they occur only in flexible packaging, do not apply to rigid containers, and cannot be measured or reproduced

questions.explanation: Natural defects caused by process failures are often large leaks or fragile leaks that are easily plugged by product; their size is hard to control and varies widely, so they are unsuitable for validation. They can still be used to understand how a method performs on real defects, and can be used together with simulated defects.

questions.question: What does TR86 require regarding positive controls and the claimed LoD of a method?

options.A: All positive controls with a leak size equal to or larger than the claimed LoD must be detected with high confidence (for example, 95%)
options.B: Only half of the positive controls larger than the LoD need to be detected; the rest can be regarded as method variation and statistical fluctuation and need not be re-verified
options.C: An average detection rate of 80% is enough, and individual defect sizes need not be reviewed, to avoid over-validation
options.D: Positive controls need only cover the largest leak size to confirm that the method can detect major defects

questions.explanation: The text states clearly that all positive controls with leaks at or above the claimed LoD must be detected with high confidence (for example, 95%). In addition, positive controls should cover both large and small leaks, including at least a set of leak sizes around the MALL and the expected LoD.

questions.question: A laboratory prepares positive controls with glass micropipettes and finds an abnormally high flow for one sample during measurement. What is the most reasonable judgment and action?

options.A: The sample is especially sensitive to the method, so it should be used first as a verification sample and tested more times to increase the detection rate
options.B: The ambient humidity is too high, so the sample only needs to be re-equilibrated with the environment and tested again, without replacing it
options.C: The defect has been blocked by product, so it should be retested at a lower pressure and this noted in the report as a normal occurrence
options.D: The micropipette tip may have broken, and the sample should no longer be used as a positive control

questions.explanation: The advantage of glass micropipettes is that they can create relatively consistent defects at small sizes, but they are fragile and the tip is easily broken during preparation; a broken tip usually gives an abnormally high flow, and such samples should not be used. The tip can be inspected under a microscope and compared against the equivalent simulated flow.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about a calibrated leak is correct?

options.A: It is a laser hole drilled directly into the wall of the product container, with one made for each batch of containers
options.B: It is calibrated against a traceable standard and housed in a robust metal casing (not a product container), and is used for routine system performance checks
options.C: Its size must always be larger than the MALL to ensure that the instrument can detect it
options.D: It can be used only with probabilistic methods; deterministic methods cannot use it

questions.explanation: A calibrated leak is a separate component with a known leak rate calibrated against an independent, traceable standard, housed in a robust metal casing and protected from blockage; it is used for routine system performance checks, and for some methods also for frequent calibration. If possible, its size should be equal to or smaller than the MALL, not larger.

questions.topic: Blockage of leak paths by protein
questions.question: CCI of a high-concentration protein drug product is tested by vacuum decay, but the positive controls show no detectable defect. According to TR86, what is the most likely cause and the appropriate response?

options.A: The protein may aggregate and block the leak path; other means should be included in the CCI strategy and seal characteristics should be monitored in stability
options.B: High-concentration protein enlarges the defect, so the detection sensitivity threshold should be raised and the test time per run shortened to avoid misjudgment
options.C: It means the container is intact with no defect, so the result can be used directly for release without any further integrity assessment
options.D: It means the test must be repeated with a substitute solution of higher viscosity, with no further assessment and no need to monitor stability

questions.explanation: In the study, a 120 mg/mL high-concentration protein solution could not flow out of the defect, while a substitute solution of the same viscosity could, which suggests that large molecules aggregate in the defect channel. Manufacturers should therefore not rely on CCIT alone to ensure sterility, but should establish a CCI strategy, such as monitoring seal properties (plunger-rib contact length, residual seal force, and so on).

questions.question: For a prefilled syringe with a staked needle, what is the requirement for assembly of the needle shield and needle?

options.A: The needle should only lightly touch the surface of the needle shield to avoid damaging the needle tip, and ensure the tip does not contact the elastomer
options.B: The needle should penetrate the needle shield completely so that both ends are sealed by elastomer, to increase sealing reliability
options.C: As long as the needle shield looks intact, there is no need to confirm the needle position and embedding depth
options.D: The needle must be fully embedded in the needle shield elastomer but must not fully penetrate it, otherwise a defect results

questions.explanation: The needle shield-needle interface is a seal between the drug product and the environment, and the part of the needle embedded in the elastomer is the most critical. The needle must be fully embedded but must not penetrate through; the drug manufacturer should confirm with the supplier that the positioning process is validated, and confirm that subsequent filling and transport do not change the position or cause puncture.

questions.question: For the combination seal and CCI testing of a multidose cartridge, what does TR86 require?

options.A: A single-layer combination seal is sufficient, because the number of punctures does not affect sealing performance and resealability
options.B: Passing the resealability test of ISO 13926-3 is regarded as completing CCI testing, with no separate verification needed
options.C: Select a bilayer elastomer with good resealability and test CCI at the maximum number of punctures
options.D: Only new, unpunctured cartridges need to be tested, because puncturing is the user's responsibility

questions.explanation: For multidose applications, a combination seal with a bilayer elastomer and robust resealing properties should be selected, and its CCI tested at the maximum number of punctures. The resealability test described in ISO 13926-3 does not constitute a CCI test, so the statement that passing it counts as completing CCI testing is a trap.

questions.question: For a plastic (polymer) prefilled syringe, who should be responsible for defining product-specific CCI requirements (such as the MALL) and ensuring that the plastic barrel and elastomer plunger form a complete system?

options.A: The supplier of the plastic barrel, because the barrel is the primary container and the supplier knows its material properties best
options.B: The marketing authorization license holder
options.C: The supplier of the elastomer plunger, because the plunger provides the seal and the supplier knows its compression properties best
options.D: The manufacturer of the CCIT instrument, because it knows the instrument's detection limit best

questions.explanation: The text states that the marketing authorization license holder is responsible for defining product-specific CCI requirements (such as the MALL) and for ensuring that the barrel and plunger form a complete system that meets the requirements. The suppliers of the plastic components are responsible for establishing and validating design requirements and CPPs; the roles are different.

questions.question: A company wants to plan testing for a single-use system (SUS). Which methods are most reasonable for the supplier's shipment release and for the user's pre-use check?

options.A: The supplier uses helium, which is more sensitive (≥ 2 µm) but complex and expensive; the user uses simple, inexpensive pressure drop (≥ 10 µm)
options.B: The supplier releases with a pressure drop technique; the user switches to helium, because the user needs the highest sensitivity
options.C: Both must use helium, because pressure drop is not a physical method, cannot give quantitative results, and cannot meet regulatory requirements
options.D: Neither needs to test; transport validation can replace testing, regardless of risk and without keeping records

questions.explanation: Helium has a sensitivity of ≥ 2 µm, but operation and maintenance are complex and the investment is high, so it suits release testing by the supplier; pressure drop has a sensitivity of ≥ 10 µm and is simpler and cheaper, and suits pre-use checks because defects larger than the MALL are more likely to occur during normal handling. The user may also evaluate replacing testing with transport validation plus visual inspection.

questions.question: After vials stored on dry ice (-80 °C) are warmed up, headspace analysis shows high CO2, low oxygen, and high total pressure. What is the most reasonable explanation?

options.A: The headspace gas was not air at filling, which is normal process parameter variation and unrelated to dry ice storage and warming
options.B: The glass vial shrinks more than the stopper at low temperature, causing permanent cracks that let gas flow in and out continuously
options.C: After warming, the contents of the vial evaporate, so oxygen is consumed, while carbon dioxide escapes from the solution
options.D: At low temperature the stopper shrinks and, below the glass transition temperature, becomes hard, so CCI is temporarily lost and outside gas enters; after warming it reseals

questions.explanation: The stopper's thermal contraction is much greater than that of glass (about 88% of volume remains at -80 °C versus about 99.5% for glass), and below its glass transition temperature it loses elasticity. The CCI failure lets CO2 from the dry ice enter, and after warming the stopper regains elasticity and reseals, causing high CO2, low O2, and high pressure. This failure is temporary, so the statement that it causes permanent cracks is wrong.

questions.question: According to TR86, what kind of test article is helium testing suitable for?

options.A: Any container with liquid leakage, including products with wet surfaces and flexible bag assemblies containing liquid
options.B: Only rigid glass containers; it cannot be used for flexible single-use bags and does not apply to plastic containers
options.C: Test articles that are dry and can withstand a pressure differential of at least 1 psi within a dedicated fixture, such as intact single-use bag assemblies
options.D: Aseptic connectors containing a porous membrane, because their helium permeation rate can serve as a built-in reference and calibration

questions.explanation: Helium testing is suitable for dry test articles that can withstand a pressure differential of at least 1 psi, and can be used for intact 2-D/3-D single-use bags and multi-bag manifolds. Components whose natural leak rate is above the limit (such as aseptic connectors containing a porous membrane) cannot be tested and must be excluded.

questions.question: What is the biggest difference between optical emission spectroscopy (OES) and helium testing when used for CCIT?

options.A: No specific tracer gas is needed; it uses the gas mixture already present in the container headspace
options.B: The container must first be filled with helium and then measured with a mass spectrometer to determine whether there is a leak
options.C: It must be performed at atmospheric pressure, cannot use vacuum, and applies only to containers of dry solid dosage forms
options.D: It is a probabilistic method whose results depend on the operator's visual interpretation, which cannot be automated and cannot quantify defect size

questions.explanation: OES needs no specific tracer gas and uses the gas already present in the container headspace; the test chamber is evacuated to low pressure (< 5×10⁻² mbar), a plasma is generated, and changes in the intensity of the emission lines of each element are analyzed. It is a deterministic, non-destructive method, so the statements that it requires helium filling and a mass spectrometer, that it must be performed at atmospheric pressure, and that it is probabilistic and visually interpreted are all incorrect.

questions.question: When using OES, under what circumstances might a leaking product be misjudged as passing? How does TR86 recommend strengthening the approach?

options.A: There is liquid behind the leak site, producing water vapor; extend the test time and purge the container with nitrogen
options.B: The leak is very large relative to container size and fill volume, so gas and water vapor are already evacuated during pump-down; combine with visual inspection to find deformed or empty containers
options.C: There is too much helium inside the container; purge with nitrogen first, then repeat the OES test and interpretation
options.D: The test container is made of glass; change to a plastic material to increase outgassing and lower the test vacuum level

questions.explanation: If the leak is too large relative to the container size and fill volume, the gas and water vapor are pumped out during the vacuum phase, no signal is present during the test phase, and the leaking product passes as if it were intact. TR86 recommends using visual inspection before or after the leak test to find deformed or empty containers. When there is liquid at the leak site, the water vapor actually shifts the detection limit to smaller orifice sizes and is not a cause of misjudgment.

questions.question: When checking pouch seals with airborne ultrasound, why can liquid inside the seal cause misjudgment?

options.A: Liquid absorbs all ultrasound, so the signal is always zero and the seal is wrongly judged a failure; the seal must be dried first
options.B: Liquid raises the heat-sealing temperature of the seal, making it look stronger, so the ultrasound signal is high and the seal is wrongly judged a pass
options.C: Ultrasound travels only through air, and liquid stops the instrument from working, so no reading can be obtained
options.D: Liquid can transmit ultrasound from one material to another, so if liquid is present in a defect, the result may resemble that of a good seal

questions.explanation: Airborne ultrasound is a through-transmission technique: a well-bonded seal lets the sound wave pass, and a defect blocks the signal. But liquid transmits ultrasound effectively, so when liquid is present in a defect the result may resemble a good seal. In addition, the sensor must be located about 2 mm to 3 mm inside the edge to obtain a useful signal, which limits inspection near the seal edge.

questions.question: How does TR86 position the role of X-ray technology in CCI assessment?

options.A: It is a deterministic leak test that quantitatively measures leak rate and can replace helium testing and other methods
options.B: It can only be used for incoming inspection of packaging materials, not for assembled products, and cannot examine internal structures
options.C: It is not a leak test but a supporting technique that can find defects that favor leakage, such as stopper misfit or glass cracks
options.D: It can determine whether gas or liquid will actually pass through a defect, so it is sufficient on its own to demonstrate sterility, with no other tests needed

questions.explanation: X-ray assesses neither the leak rate nor the leak itself, quantitatively or qualitatively; at the present stage it is best used as a supporting technique to show physical attributes that are hard to see visually (such as stopper misfit and glass cracks). It cannot determine whether gas or liquid will actually flow through a defect, and is often used together with true leak tests such as helium or headspace analysis.

questions.question: In transport and distribution, why are small defects such as checks, cracks, and chips more of a concern than vial breakage?

options.A: Because vial breakage does not affect the product and can be ignored
options.B: Because small defects are not easily noticed by users, can affect quality, and may grow into liquid loss or microbial ingress during later distribution
options.C: Because small defects occur only in secondary packaging and have nothing to do with the primary package
options.D: Because the ISTA and ASTM standards cannot simulate any form of physical stress

questions.explanation: Large defects such as vial breakage are easy to notice and usually prevent the product from being used, whereas leaks from small defects may affect quality without being noticed by users; a check may become a crack and a crack may widen, so they are a latent risk. Secondary and tertiary packaging must also be considered, and ASTM and ISTA have standards that can simulate various distribution scenarios.

questions.question: A product will be shipped by air, with limited pressure control in the cargo hold. In terms of package integrity, what does TR86 require to be specifically evaluated?

options.A: Nothing about pressure differential needs evaluating as long as the product temperature meets specification, because pressure changes do not affect package integrity
options.B: Only rigid glass vials need evaluation; flexible containers are unaffected, and prefilled syringes need no evaluation of pressure and altitude changes
options.C: Only a visual inspection after arrival at the destination is needed, with no evaluation of any effect of pressure differential on the package
options.D: The resistance of flexible containers to creep or burst, and plunger movement of prefilled syringes at low pressure

questions.explanation: The cargo hold on an aircraft may be partly or completely unpressurized, so the pressure differential needs to be evaluated. Examples include whether sealed flexible containers resist creep or burst, and backward movement of the plunger in a prefilled syringe, which may move the seal and product into a non-sterile region and, in extreme cases, push the plunger out completely.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about 100% in-line CCIT is consistent with TR86?

options.A: A package that passes in-line testing is not guaranteed to maintain CCI over shelf life; one that is rejected is guaranteed not to meet requirements
options.B: Regulations require 100% in-line testing of all products, which must be explained in the submission
options.C: As long as in-line testing is in place, off-line QC testing and other control measures are not needed
options.D: Current technology can achieve 100% in-line testing for all CCS and product types, without any limitation

questions.explanation: An in-line test station acts like a filter that rejects defective units and reduces CCI failures caused by random process failures, but passing does not guarantee that CCI is maintained throughout shelf life. A regulatory requirement for 100% inspection exists only for containers sealed by fusion during in-line filling, such as ampoules and BFS; for other products it should be decided by an ICH Q9 risk assessment, and in-line testing should not be the only control point.

questions.question: A QC analyst removes a sample from the process line, isolates it from the process stream, and analyzes it beside the line. According to TR86, what type of testing is this?

options.A: In-line, because the sample did not leave the process stream
options.B: On-line, because a sample diverted out is always returned to the process stream
options.C: At-line, where the sample is removed, isolated, and analyzed
options.D: Off-line, because all removed samples are analyzed in a laboratory

questions.explanation: At-line means the sample is removed and isolated from the process stream and then analyzed. In in-line testing the sample does not leave the process stream and the test is non-destructive; in on-line testing the sample is diverted and may be returned to the process stream; off-line testing does not involve sampling directly from the manufacturing line, usually takes place in a laboratory, and is not high-speed. When 100% testing is required, an in-line or on-line method is usually needed.

questions.question: In the hypothetical PharmaCo-A study, Test Method C detected only 92.5% of defects larger than 10 µm on Day 2, yet the detection limit was still confirmed as 10 µm in the end. What is the reason?

options.A: Follow-up investigation found that the three missed defects had been blocked, so that data point was excluded and the detection limit was confirmed
options.B: The company temporarily lowered the acceptance criterion from 95% to 90% and recalculated the overall detection rate to meet the specification
options.C: The company switched to a smaller sample size, so the statistical result was no longer representative and did not affect the conclusion
options.D: The company attributed Day 2 to operator error and deleted all the negative control data before reanalyzing

questions.explanation: PharmaCo-A had pre-defined the detection limit as the size at which defects are detected at a rate of 95% or more on all test days, and all larger defects must also be detected. The three defects not detected on Day 2 were found on investigation to be blocked, so the data were excluded, which confirmed the 10 µm limit and the method's accuracy. However, because of the large day-to-day variation, the company still questioned the reliability of Method C and put it on hold.
